checklist.title: Falsify secp256r1 precompile return value format consistency across execution paths
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Deploy a contract that calls the secp256r1 precompile (0x0b / address TBD per EIP-7951) with a valid signature and checks returndata size == 32 and returndata == 0x0000...0001. 2. Deploy a second contract that calls with invalid signature (wrong r, s, or public key) and checks returndata size == 0. 3. Execute both transactions in a block and verify all client implementations produce identical return values. 4. Edge cases: (a) valid signature but point-at-infinity public key, (b) signature with s > n/2 (malleability), (c) zero-length input, (d) input shorter than 160 bytes. 5. Compare return values across at least two EL client implementations.
executable_checks: Create test transaction calling precompile with valid (r, s, x, y, hash) and assert returndata == bytes32(1)
Create test transaction calling precompile with invalid signature and assert returndata == bytes(0)
Fuzz input lengths from 0 to 200 bytes and verify consistent return across clients
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7951-POSTCOND-001. Post-condition check. Divergent return formats across clients would cause consensus split on any block containing a secp256r1 precompile call. Covers nodes: ACTION-RETURN-SUCCESS, ACTION-RETURN-EMPTY, STATE-PRECOMPILE-COMPLETE.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for future-slot block rejection in fork choice
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a signed beacon block with slot = get_current_slot(store) + 1 (one slot in the future). 2. Send this block via P2P gossip to a target node. 3. Verify the block is rejected by the fork choice store (on_block should fail the slot check). 4. Test boundary: slot exactly equal to current slot (should be accepted). 5. Test slot = current_slot + SECONDS_PER_SLOT (edge of tolerance). 6. Verify no state mutation occurs when the future block is rejected.
executable_checks: Send block with slot = current_slot + 1 via P2P and verify rejection
Send block with slot = current_slot and verify acceptance (if otherwise valid)
Verify store state is unchanged after future block rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-PRECOND-002. Boundary property. Covers edges: EDGE-PARENT-OK-TO-SLOT, EDGE-SLOT-FAIL. An attacker sending future-dated blocks via P2P could manipulate fork choice if the slot check is bypassed.

checklist.title: Falsify deep copy isolation between parent and child beacon states
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Obtain a reference to the parent beacon state from the fork choice store. 2. Execute on_block which copies the parent state and applies state_transition. 3. After state_transition completes, compare the parent state in the store with a snapshot taken before the operation. 4. Specifically check mutable nested structures: (a) validator registry entries, (b) balances array, (c) slashings array, (d) participation flags, (e) proposer_lookahead array (new in Fulu). 5. Modify the child state and verify parent state is unaffected. 6. Language-specific: check for reference sharing in Python (id() comparison), Go (pointer comparison), Rust (Rc/Arc sharing).
executable_checks: Snapshot parent state hash before on_block, verify unchanged after
Mutate child state validator balance, verify parent validator balance unchanged
Check proposer_lookahead array in child vs parent for reference independence
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-INV-001. Invariant falsification. Covers nodes: STATE-PARENT-STATE-COPIED, ACTION-STATE-TRANSITION-EXEC. Shallow copy bug would corrupt the fork choice store across blocks, affecting all subsequent fork choice decisions.

checklist.title: Falsify determinism of proposer lookahead computation across clients
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a beacon state at an epoch boundary with a known RANDAO mix and a set of active validators with specific effective balances. 2. Call get_beacon_proposer_index for each slot in the epoch on at least two different client implementations. 3. Compare the proposer indices slot-by-slot. 4. Edge cases: (a) all validators have MIN_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE, (b) one validator has MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE and rest have minimum, (c) validators at activation/exit epoch boundaries, (d) large validator set (>1M validators). 5. Verify the compute_proposer_index shuffle uses the correct domain separation for Fulu.
executable_checks: Compute proposer indices for a full epoch on two clients with identical state, compare results
Test with validators at activation_epoch == current_epoch boundary
Verify RANDAO domain separation includes Fulu fork version
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7917-INV-002. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7917-03. EIP-7917 introduces deterministic proposer lookahead; non-determinism would cause network-wide consensus failure.

checklist.title: Falsify active validator set filtering for proposer lookahead
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Create a beacon state with validators in various lifecycle stages: active, pending activation, exiting (exit_epoch == current_epoch + 1), exited, slashed. 2. Compute the proposer lookahead for the next epoch. 3. Verify that only validators with is_active_validator(validator, target_epoch) == True appear in the lookahead. 4. Edge case: validator whose exit_epoch == target_epoch (should still be active). 5. Edge case: validator whose activation_epoch == target_epoch (should be active). 6. Edge case: mass exit scenario where >50% of validators are exiting.
executable_checks: Verify exited validators (exit_epoch < target_epoch) never appear in lookahead
Verify pending validators (activation_epoch > target_epoch) never appear in lookahead
Test mass exit scenario: ensure no empty proposer slots
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7917-INV-005. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7917-01. Including inactive validators in selection causes missed slots.

checklist.title: Falsify verify_block=True enforcement in fork choice on_block
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Inspect the on_block handler code path in the fork choice implementation. 2. Verify that state_transition is called with verify_block=True (or equivalent full verification flag). 3. Create a deliberately invalid block (e.g., invalid proposer signature, invalid state root) and submit it to on_block. 4. Verify the block is rejected. 5. Check for any code paths where state_transition might be called with verification disabled (e.g., optimistic sync, checkpoint sync). 6. Specifically check Fulu-specific additions: does the new proposer_lookahead processing affect the verification path?
executable_checks: Submit block with invalid proposer signature to on_block, verify rejection
Submit block with invalid state_root, verify rejection
Code audit: grep for state_transition calls with verify_block=False in fork choice paths
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-POSTCOND-005. Post-condition falsification. If verify_block is accidentally disabled, any invalid block would be accepted into the fork choice store, corrupting all subsequent chain state.

checklist.title: Falsify minimum custody group assignment guarantee (CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT >= 4)
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Generate a large set of random node_ids (at least 10,000). 2. For each node_id, call get_custody_groups(node_id) or equivalent. 3. Verify len(result) >= CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (4) for every node_id. 4. Edge cases: (a) node_id = 0, (b) node_id = 2^256 - 1, (c) node_id values that produce hash collisions in the custody group computation. 5. Verify the total number of unique groups across all node_ids covers all NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS groups.
executable_checks: Enumerate 10,000 random node_ids, verify min custody group count >= 4
Test node_id = 0 and node_id = max_uint256
Verify union of all custody groups covers full group range
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-DASCORE-INV-002. Invariant falsification. Under-assigned custody groups reduce data availability coverage.

checklist.title: Falsify equivalence of reconstructed and gossip-received column handling
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Obtain a set of data columns via gossip for a known block. 2. Independently reconstruct the same columns from sufficient erasure-coded pieces. 3. Compare the internal representation: (a) data content must be byte-identical, (b) metadata (block_root, column_index, slot) must match, (c) KZG proofs must be identical. 4. Verify both gossip-received and reconstructed columns pass the same validation pipeline. 5. Check if any internal flags or status fields differentiate reconstructed from received columns (they should not for downstream processing).
executable_checks: Reconstruct columns and compare byte-for-byte with gossip-received equivalents
Verify reconstructed columns pass the same is_data_available check
Check internal data structures for any differentiation between sources
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-DASCORE-INV-005. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-DAS-CORE-04. Inconsistent treatment could cause DA sampling failures.

checklist.title: Falsify Fusaka fork identifier correctness after activation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set up a node configured for Fusaka fork at a specific epoch. 2. Advance the node past the fork epoch. 3. Query the node's fork_id (via devp2p Status message or internal API). 4. Verify the fork_id matches the expected value: CRC32 of genesis hash XOR'd with fork block number/timestamp. 5. For mainnet: verify fork_id == 0x5167e2a6 (or whatever the final value is). 6. Cross-check: connect two nodes post-fork and verify they successfully peer (matching fork_ids). 7. Cross-check: connect a pre-fork and post-fork node and verify they reject each other.
executable_checks: Verify fork_id value matches specification after fork activation
Verify two post-fork nodes can peer successfully
Verify pre-fork and post-fork nodes reject peering
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7607-POSTCOND-001. Post-condition falsification. Wrong fork ID would isolate nodes on the network. Covers nodes: ACTION-UPDATE-FORK-ID, STATE-FUSAKA-ACTIVE.

checklist.title: Falsify 2 MiB safety margin between MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE and CL MAX_BLOCK_SIZE
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct an EL block that is exactly MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) in serialized RLP form. 2. Wrap this EL block in a beacon block (SignedBeaconBlock) with maximum-size attestations, sync committee, and blob KZG commitments. 3. Measure the total serialized size of the beacon block. 4. Verify total size < MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (10 MiB). 5. The difference must be >= 2 MiB to maintain the safety margin. 6. Edge case: maximum number of blob_kzg_commitments (max_blobs_per_block) combined with maximum EL block size.
executable_checks: Construct max-size EL block (8 MiB RLP), wrap in beacon block, verify total < 10 MiB
Compute worst-case beacon block wrapper overhead with max blob commitments
Verify 2 MiB margin holds under all parameter combinations
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7934-INV-002. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7934-02, assumption: ASSUM-EIP7934-01. If safety margin is insufficient, valid EL blocks get rejected at CL.

checklist.title: Falsify independence and unpredictability of transaction role assignment PRNG
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Observe a node's role decisions (provider vs sampler) for a sequence of transaction announcements from the same peer. 2. Perform statistical tests: (a) chi-squared test for uniform distribution, (b) serial correlation test for sequential dependence, (c) runs test for randomness. 3. Attempt to predict future role decisions based on observed history (if PRNG is seeded with predictable inputs like peer_id or tx_hash). 4. Check if the announcing peer can influence the seed (e.g., by choosing specific tx hashes). 5. Verify the PRNG source is cryptographically secure (not math/rand or similar).
executable_checks: Collect 1000+ role decisions, run chi-squared test for uniformity
Attempt prediction of next role decision from observed sequence
Audit PRNG source: verify CSPRNG usage, not deterministic seed from peer-controlled data
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8070-INV-001. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP8070-01. If role is predictable, attacker can target providers to suppress data availability.

checklist.title: Falsify blob inclusion policy correctness for conservative/optimistic/proactive modes
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set up a proposer node with each blob inclusion policy (conservative, optimistic, proactive). 2. For conservative: provide a blob that has full local data but has NOT been sampled. Verify it IS included. Provide a blob with only sampling confirmation. Verify it is NOT included. 3. For optimistic: provide a blob that passed sampling. Verify it IS included. Provide a blob that has NOT been sampled. Verify it is NOT included. 4. For proactive: provide a blob that passed sampling previously. Verify re-sampling occurs before inclusion. 5. Verify that no policy includes blobs with zero availability evidence.
executable_checks: Conservative mode: verify only full-local-data blobs are included
Optimistic mode: verify only sampled blobs are included
Proactive mode: verify re-sampling occurs before proposal
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8070-INV-004. Invariant falsification. Including unavailable blobs causes DA verification failure network-wide.

checklist.title: Falsify eth/69 Status message field correctness on handshake
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Initiate an eth/69 handshake from a test node to a target node. 2. Capture the Status message sent by the target. 3. Verify all fields are present and well-formed: version (must be 69), networkid, genesis hash, forkid, earliestBlock (new in eth/69, replaces TD), latestBlock, latestBlockHash. 4. Verify earliestBlock matches the node's actual earliest available block (post-history-expiry). 5. Edge case: node just started, has not yet synced — verify defaults are correct. 6. Verify the removed fields (TD, totalDifficulty) are NOT present.
executable_checks: Capture eth/69 Status message and verify all required fields present
Verify earliestBlock field is accurate
Verify totalDifficulty field is absent (removed in eth/69)
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-EIP7642-HANDSHAKE-PRECOND-04. Pre-condition falsification. Malformed status messages cause peer isolation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for eth/69 compact receipt decoding from untrusted peers
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a Receipts response via eth/69 P2P containing malformed compact receipts: (a) missing tx-type field, (b) extra fields beyond [tx-type, post-state-or-status, cumulative-gas, logs], (c) bloom filter included (should not be in compact format), (d) negative cumulative-gas, (e) oversized logs array. 2. Verify target node rejects all malformed receipts without crashing. 3. Verify valid compact receipts (without bloom) are accepted. 4. Fuzz the RLP encoding with random mutations to detect parser crashes.
executable_checks: Send receipt with bloom filter included (old format), verify rejection
Send receipt with missing fields, verify rejection without crash
RLP fuzz compact receipt format with 1000 random mutations
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-EIP7642-RECEIPT-PRECOND-02. Boundary property. Trust boundary: untrusted peer data crosses into receipt decoder. Malformed receipt parsing could cause crashes or memory corruption.

checklist.title: Falsify parent-seen check for data column sidecar gossip validation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a valid data_column_sidecar referencing a parent_root that the target node has NOT seen. 2. Send it via gossip. 3. Verify the node IGNOREs the sidecar (does not process it, does not store it). 4. Then send the actual parent block, followed by the sidecar again. 5. Verify the sidecar is now accepted. 6. Edge case: send sidecar referencing a parent from an alternate fork that was later pruned.
executable_checks: Send sidecar with unknown parent_root, verify IGNORE
Send parent block then re-send sidecar, verify acceptance
Verify no state changes from ignored sidecars
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-GOSSIP-PRECOND-06. Pre-condition falsification. Parent check prevents orphan processing.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for DataColumnSidecarsByRange request parameter validation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a DataColumnSidecarsByRange request with: (a) count = MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS + 1 (exceeds limit), (b) start_slot = 0, count = 2^64-1 (overflow), (c) columns list containing duplicate indices, (d) columns list containing out-of-range indices (>= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS), (e) empty columns list. 2. Verify each request is rejected with appropriate error and does not cause resource exhaustion. 3. Measure response time for valid large requests near the limit. 4. Verify the node rate-limits repeated large requests from the same peer.
executable_checks: Send request with count exceeding MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS, verify rejection
Send request with overflow values, verify no crash
Send request with out-of-range column indices, verify rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-REQRESP-PRECOND-01. Boundary property. Trust boundary: untrusted peer sends request parameters. Unbounded requests could exhaust disk I/O and memory.

checklist.title: Falsify peer custody compliance monitoring and enforcement
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Connect a malicious peer that advertises custody of specific column groups in its ENR. 2. Request columns from the advertised custody groups. 3. Have the malicious peer fail to respond or return errors. 4. Verify the target node: (a) detects the non-compliance, (b) downscores the peer, (c) eventually disconnects the peer. 5. Verify the node seeks alternative peers for the missing custody groups. 6. Test timing: how long before non-compliant peer is penalized?
executable_checks: Connect non-compliant peer, verify downscore after failed custody requests
Verify eventual disconnection of non-compliant peer
Verify node finds replacement peer for uncovered custody groups
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-DISCOVERY-POSTCOND-01. Post-condition falsification. Failure to enforce custody allows free-riding peers degrading DA capacity.

checklist.title: Falsify retroactive fork upgrade state consistency for syncing nodes
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set up a 'live' node that processes the Fulu fork epoch in real-time. 2. Record the post-fork state root at the first Fulu slot. 3. Set up a 'syncing' node that starts from a pre-fork checkpoint and replays blocks through the fork epoch. 4. Compare the syncing node's state root at the same slot with the live node's. 5. They must be identical. 6. Specifically verify: (a) proposer_lookahead array initialization, (b) any new Fulu state fields, (c) validator registry state after upgrade.
executable_checks: Compare state roots between live and syncing nodes at first Fulu slot
Verify proposer_lookahead initialization is identical on both paths
Verify all new Fulu state fields match between live and synced nodes
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-FORK-TRANSITION-INV-003. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-FULU-FORK-01. Syncing nodes must produce identical post-fork state.

checklist.title: Falsify get_blob_parameters completeness for all post-Electra epochs
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call get_blob_parameters for: (a) epoch == ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH, (b) epoch == FULU_FORK_EPOCH - 1, (c) epoch == FULU_FORK_EPOCH, (d) epoch == FULU_FORK_EPOCH + 1, (e) epoch = far future (e.g., 2^32). 2. Verify all calls return valid BlobParameters (never None/null/error). 3. Verify Electra-era epochs return Electra defaults (target=3, max=6). 4. Verify Fulu-era epochs return correct updated parameters from BLOB_SCHEDULE. 5. Edge case: epoch between two BLOB_SCHEDULE entries — verify correct interpolation or lookup. 6. Edge case: empty BLOB_SCHEDULE — verify fallback to Electra defaults.
executable_checks: Call get_blob_parameters for every boundary epoch, verify non-null return
Verify Electra-era epochs return target=3, max=6
Verify Fulu-era epochs return updated parameters
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-BLOB-SCHEDULE-INV-001. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-FULU-BEACON-01. Missing blob params causes block validation failure or acceptance of invalid blocks.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for blob_kzg_commitments count validation on P2P blocks
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Determine max_blobs_per_block for the current epoch via get_blob_parameters(). 2. Construct a beacon block with blob_kzg_commitments count = max_blobs_per_block + 1. 3. Send via P2P gossip. 4. Verify rejection at gossip validation (before state transition). 5. Test with exactly max_blobs_per_block commitments — should be accepted. 6. Test across a BLOB_SCHEDULE epoch boundary where max changes — verify the correct limit is applied based on the block's epoch, not the current epoch.
executable_checks: Send block with max_blobs + 1 commitments, verify rejection
Send block with exactly max_blobs commitments, verify acceptance
Test at BLOB_SCHEDULE epoch boundary with changing max
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-EXEC-PAYLOAD-PRE-001. Boundary property. Trust boundary: P2P peer sends block with attacker-controlled blob commitment count. Maps to EDGE-PEER-BLOCK-TO-CL-VALIDATION.

checklist.title: Verify dynamic blob commitment limit uses epoch-correct parameters
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify the blob commitment check calls get_blob_parameters with the block's epoch (get_current_epoch(state)), not a hardcoded value. 2. At a BLOB_SCHEDULE transition epoch, verify blocks at epoch N use limit_N and blocks at epoch N+1 use limit_N+1. 3. Verify the check is len(commitments) <= max, not len(commitments) < max.
executable_checks: Verify get_blob_parameters is called with block's epoch
Test boundary block at schedule transition epoch
Verify <= vs < comparison correctness
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-EXEC-PAYLOAD-PRE-001. Supporting node check for boundary property. Ensures internal logic correctly computes the dynamic limit.

checklist.title: Falsify blob base fee reserve price floor enforcement
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a block header sequence where the natural blob base fee (from EIP-4844 mechanism) drops below BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee_per_gas / GAS_PER_BLOB. 2. Verify the reserve pricing mode activates (excess_blob_gas computation changes). 3. Test boundary: blob_base_fee exactly equals the reserve price. 4. Verify the comparison uses >= or > correctly per spec. 5. Compute excess_blob_gas under both pricing modes and verify the correct mode is selected. 6. Cross-check with at least two EL clients.
executable_checks: Construct block where blob fee < reserve price, verify reserve mode activates
Test exact boundary where blob fee == reserve price
Compare excess_blob_gas computation across two EL clients
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-EIP7918-RESERVE-INV-001. Invariant falsification. Wrong pricing mode produces different excess_blob_gas, causing consensus split.

checklist.title: Falsify EIP-7918 constant values (BLOB_BASE_COST and GAS_PER_BLOB)
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. In each EL client implementation, locate the BLOB_BASE_COST constant definition. 2. Verify BLOB_BASE_COST == 8192 (2^13). 3. Locate GAS_PER_BLOB constant. Verify GAS_PER_BLOB == 131072 (2^17). 4. Compute the ratio: BLOB_BASE_COST / GAS_PER_BLOB. Verify it equals 1/16. 5. Cross-check across all EL client implementations (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Reth, Erigon). 6. Verify no integer overflow in reserve price calculation: BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee_per_gas (could overflow uint64 at high base fees).
executable_checks: Verify BLOB_BASE_COST == 8192 in each client
Verify GAS_PER_BLOB == 131072 in each client
Check for integer overflow in BLOB_BASE_COST * max_possible_base_fee_per_gas
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-EIP7918-RESERVE-INV-003. Invariant falsification. Wrong constants would affect every block's fee calculation, causing immediate consensus split.

checklist.title: Falsify proposer lookahead ordering after all other epoch processing steps
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Inspect the process_epoch function in each CL client. 2. Verify process_proposer_lookahead (or equivalent) is called AFTER: (a) process_justification_and_finalization, (b) process_rewards_and_penalties, (c) process_slashings, (d) process_sync_committee_updates. 3. Construct a test case where rewards/slashings change the active validator set. 4. Compute the lookahead with correct ordering vs incorrect ordering (before rewards). 5. Verify the results differ, confirming ordering matters. 6. Check all CL clients for consistent ordering.
executable_checks: Audit process_epoch call order in each CL client
Construct state where rewards change active set, verify lookahead depends on order
Compare lookahead results with correct vs incorrect ordering
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-EPOCH-PROC-INV-002. Invariant falsification. Wrong ordering produces different proposer assignments on all buggy nodes.

checklist.title: Falsify correct parent block data retrieval for reserve price computation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. During block validation, verify the parent block's base_fee_per_gas, excess_blob_gas, and blob_gas_used are read from the correct parent (by parent_hash). 2. Test with a reorg scenario: ensure the correct parent is used after chain reorganization. 3. Verify no caching issues: if the parent was previously read for a different fork, ensure fresh data is used. 4. Edge case: genesis block as parent (no excess_blob_gas). 5. Edge case: first block after Fulu fork (parent is last Electra block).
executable_checks: Verify parent data matches parent_hash, not just previous block number
Test after reorg: verify correct parent data is used
Test first Fulu block reading Electra parent data
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-EIP7918-RESERVE-PRE-003. Pre-condition falsification. Wrong parent data produces incorrect fee calculations for all subsequent blocks.

checklist.title: Falsify EL-CL fork activation alignment for Blob Parameter Only hardforks
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Examine the EIP-7892 specification for BPO fork activation. 2. Verify the EL activation timestamp and CL activation epoch map to the same slot boundary. 3. Compute: CL_activation_slot = FULU_FORK_EPOCH * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH. Expected_timestamp = GENESIS_TIME + CL_activation_slot * SECONDS_PER_SLOT. 4. Verify EL activation timestamp equals Expected_timestamp. 5. Test the window between CL and EL activation if they don't align: submit a block with new blob params on one layer while old params on the other. 6. Verify validation is consistent across both layers.
executable_checks: Compute expected EL timestamp from CL epoch, verify match
Test block at exact activation boundary with both old and new blob params
Verify no validation mismatch window between EL and CL
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W4-EIP7892-PRECOND-004. Pre-condition falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7892-02. NOTE: exploitability=configuration-error but in-scope; requires further investigation of spec-level guarantees.

checklist.title: Falsify EIP-7883 gas >= EIP-2565 gas for all MODEXP inputs
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Implement both the EIP-2565 and EIP-7883 gas formulas. 2. For each input combination (base_length, exponent_length, modulus_length) in ranges [0, 1024]: compute both gas costs. 3. Verify EIP-7883 >= EIP-2565 for ALL combinations. 4. Focus on edge cases: (a) very small inputs (all lengths = 1), (b) inputs near the new upper bounds (EIP-7823), (c) exponent with leading zeros, (d) exponent = 0, (e) modulus_length = 1 (minimum). 5. Use property-based testing (e.g., Hypothesis/QuickCheck) to search for counterexamples.
executable_checks: Compare EIP-7883 vs EIP-2565 gas for all (base_len, exp_len, mod_len) in [0, 32]
Property-based fuzz: random inputs in [0, 1024], assert EIP-7883 >= EIP-2565
Test specific edge: exponent = 0, modulus_length = 1
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W4-EIP7883-INV-002. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7883-01. Gas regression enables DoS via underpriced computation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for column index validation on received P2P samples
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a data column sample via P2P with column_index = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS (one past the valid range). 2. Send a sample with column_index = 2^64 - 1 (max uint64). 3. Send a sample with column_index = -1 (if signed type). 4. Verify each is rejected without crash or panic. 5. Verify valid column_index in [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS-1] is accepted. 6. Monitor for memory corruption or array bounds violations (use address sanitizer if possible).
executable_checks: Send sample with column_index = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS, verify rejection
Send sample with column_index = MAX_UINT64, verify no crash
Verify valid column_index is accepted
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-DAS-PRECOND-002. Boundary property. Trust boundary: untrusted P2P peer provides column indices. Out-of-range indices could crash nodes or corrupt custody tracking.

checklist.title: Verify column index validation occurs before any array indexing or storage
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Audit the sample processing code path: verify column_index bounds check is the first validation step, before any array access using the index. 2. Check for TOCTOU: ensure the index is not modified between validation and use. 3. Verify the bounds check uses NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS from the current configuration, not a hardcoded value.
executable_checks: Code audit: verify bounds check precedes array access
Verify NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS is not hardcoded but derived from config
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-DAS-PRECOND-002. Supporting node check. Ensures validation ordering prevents exploitation.

checklist.title: Falsify timeout enforcement on column sampling requests to peers
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set up a malicious peer that accepts column sample requests but never responds. 2. Request columns from this peer. 3. Measure how long the requesting node waits before timing out. 4. Verify a timeout exists and is reasonable (e.g., < 10 seconds). 5. Verify the node: (a) marks the request as failed after timeout, (b) tries an alternative peer, (c) does not leak resources (open connections, memory). 6. Test with multiple concurrent stalling peers to verify the node doesn't block all DA sampling.
executable_checks: Connect stalling peer, verify timeout fires within reasonable bound
Verify node retries with alternative peer after timeout
Connect multiple stalling peers, verify DA sampling still progresses
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-DAS-AMB-003. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7594-03. Must demonstrate single-connection stalling, not sustained DoS.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for KZG verification before erasure code reconstruction
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Provide sufficient columns (>= 50%) for reconstruction, but include one column with invalid data (modified cell content but original KZG proof). 2. Verify the individual KZG verification catches the invalid column BEFORE reconstruction begins. 3. Test: provide a column with a valid KZG proof for different data (proof from column X applied to column Y). 4. Test: provide a column with all-zero proof. 5. Verify reconstruction does NOT proceed with any unverified column. 6. Verify the corrupted reconstruction result (if verification is skipped) would propagate incorrect blob data.
executable_checks: Supply column with mismatched data/proof, verify rejection before reconstruction
Supply column with proof from different column, verify rejection
Verify reconstruction only uses KZG-verified columns
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-RECON-PRECOND-001. Boundary property. Trust boundary: P2P peer provides columns for reconstruction. Corrupted reconstruction could propagate incorrect blob data to the network.

checklist.title: Verify reconstruction output is re-verified against blob KZG commitments
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. After reconstruction completes, verify the reconstructed blob data is validated against the original blob_kzg_commitments from the beacon block. 2. If any reconstructed blob fails KZG commitment verification, verify the entire reconstruction is rejected. 3. This is a defense-in-depth check: even if individual column KZG passes, the full blob commitment must also be verified.
executable_checks: Verify post-reconstruction KZG commitment check exists
Supply valid-KZG columns that reconstruct to wrong blob, verify rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-RECON-PRECOND-001. Supporting node check. Defense-in-depth: reconstruction output must be verified against blob commitments.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for MODEXP modulus length upper bound enforcement
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Submit a transaction calling MODEXP precompile (address 0x05) with modulus_length = 1025 bytes (one over the 1024 limit). 2. Verify the precompile returns empty (rejects) before performing any computation. 3. Test with modulus_length = 1024 (should succeed). 4. Test with modulus_length = 0 (edge case). 5. Test with modulus_length = 2^32 - 1 (max uint32, if length is 32-bit). 6. Measure execution time for modulus_length = 1024 vs 1025: the 1025 case must return instantly (no computation). 7. Test all three input lengths (base, exponent, modulus) against their respective bounds.
executable_checks: Submit MODEXP with modulus_length = 1025, verify immediate rejection
Submit MODEXP with modulus_length = 1024, verify success
Measure execution time: 1025 must be near-zero (no computation)
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7823-VAL-PRECOND-003. Boundary property. Trust boundary: attacker-controlled calldata via on-chain transaction. Unbounded modulus causes excessive computation potentially crashing all clients.

checklist.title: Verify MODEXP length check applies to base and exponent lengths too
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Per EIP-7823, verify upper bounds apply to ALL three lengths: base_length <= 1024, exponent_length <= 1024, modulus_length <= 1024. 2. Test: base_length = 1025 with modulus_length = 1024. 3. Test: exponent_length = 1025 with modulus_length = 1024. 4. Verify all are rejected. 5. Verify the checks are performed in the correct order (before gas deduction).
executable_checks: Submit MODEXP with base_length = 1025, verify rejection
Submit MODEXP with exponent_length = 1025, verify rejection
Verify all length checks occur before gas deduction
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7823-VAL-PRECOND-003. Supporting node check. All three input length bounds must be enforced per EIP-7823.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for transaction gas limit cap enforcement at mempool
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Submit a transaction with gasLimit = 16,777,217 (2^24 + 1) via P2P. 2. Verify it is rejected at mempool acceptance. 3. Submit a transaction with gasLimit = 16,777,216 (2^24). Verify it is accepted. 4. Submit a transaction with gasLimit = 16,777,215 (2^24 - 1). Verify it is accepted. 5. Test all transaction types: legacy (type 0), EIP-2930 (type 1), EIP-1559 (type 2), EIP-4844 (type 3). 6. Verify the error message indicates gas limit cap violation.
executable_checks: Submit tx with gasLimit = 2^24 + 1, verify mempool rejection
Submit tx with gasLimit = 2^24, verify acceptance
Test all tx types (0, 1, 2, 3) with over-cap gasLimit
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7825-TX-PRECOND-001. Boundary property. Trust boundary: attacker submits transaction via P2P with controlled gasLimit. Over-cap transactions could cause resource exhaustion.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for dual gas cap enforcement at mempool AND block validation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a block containing a transaction with gasLimit = 2^24 + 1 (bypassing mempool, created by a malicious block producer). 2. Submit this block via P2P. 3. Verify the block is REJECTED at block validation (not just mempool). 4. Verify the rejection occurs before executing the transaction. 5. Check: does the block validation path independently check per-tx gas limits? Or does it rely on mempool having already validated? 6. Code audit: verify there is an explicit gas limit cap check in the block validation path, separate from mempool.
executable_checks: Submit block with over-cap tx (bypass mempool), verify block rejection
Code audit: verify block validation has independent gas cap check
Verify rejection occurs before tx execution
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7825-SEC-INV-001. Boundary property. Trust boundary: malicious block producer includes over-cap tx in block. Missing block-level enforcement allows complete bypass of the gas cap. Dual enforcement at both layers is critical.

checklist.title: Falsify fork upgrade application during state replay at FULU_FORK_EPOCH boundary
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Start a node from a pre-fork checkpoint state. 2. Replay blocks through the FULU_FORK_EPOCH boundary. 3. Verify upgrade_to_fulu is called at exactly the correct slot (FULU_FORK_EPOCH * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH). 4. Verify the upgrade is applied regardless of syncing mode (full sync, checkpoint sync, optimistic sync). 5. Compare post-upgrade state root with a reference node that was live during the fork. 6. Test: skip the fork epoch slot entirely (empty slot). Verify the upgrade still applies at the epoch boundary.
executable_checks: Replay through fork epoch, verify upgrade_to_fulu is called at correct slot
Test with empty slot at fork epoch, verify upgrade still applies
Compare post-upgrade state root with reference
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-FORK-ST-PRECOND-002. Pre-condition falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-FULU-FORK-01. Nodes that skip the fork during sync would fork off the main chain.

checklist.title: Falsify Merkle inclusion proof validity in constructed DataColumnSidecars
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct DataColumnSidecars from a known block with blob transactions. 2. For each sidecar, independently verify the Merkle inclusion proof against the signed block header's body_root. 3. Verify the proof path includes: (a) correct generalized index for blob_kzg_commitments, (b) correct tree depth, (c) correct leaf hash. 4. Test with different numbers of blobs (1, max_blobs_per_block). 5. Test with different column indices (0, mid, max). 6. Submit the constructed sidecars to a receiving node and verify they pass gossip validation.
executable_checks: Verify Merkle proof for each sidecar against block body_root
Test with 1 blob and max blobs
Submit sidecars to receiving node, verify gossip acceptance
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-VAL-SIDECAR-POSTCOND-001. Post-condition falsification. Invalid Merkle proofs cause receiving peers to reject all sidecars, breaking data availability for the block.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for full DataColumnSidecar validation on P2P gossip
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a crafted DataColumnSidecar via P2P pubsub with: (a) invalid KZG proof, (b) invalid Merkle inclusion proof, (c) column_index >= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS, (d) slot in the far future, (e) invalid proposer signature. 2. For each case, verify the sidecar is REJECTED. 3. Test bypass: valid KZG proof but invalid Merkle proof (and vice versa). 4. Test bypass: all proofs valid but for a different block (replay attack). 5. Verify the validation order prevents early exit before all checks complete. 6. Monitor for any crash, panic, or undefined behavior on malformed input.
executable_checks: Send sidecar with invalid KZG proof, verify rejection
Send sidecar with invalid Merkle proof but valid KZG, verify rejection
Send sidecar with out-of-range column_index, verify rejection without crash
Send sidecar with invalid proposer signature, verify rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-VAL-TRUST-PRECOND-001. Boundary property. Trust boundary: unauthenticated P2P peers send arbitrary crafted sidecars. This is the PRIMARY attack surface for PeerDAS. Missing validation could lead to state corruption or crashes across all vulnerable nodes.

checklist.title: Falsify EIP-6110 implementation completeness before history expiry activation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify the CL client processes deposits via EIP-6110 (in-protocol deposits from execution layer) rather than reading deposit contract logs from historical EL data. 2. After history expiry: attempt to process a new validator deposit. Verify it succeeds via EIP-6110. 3. Verify the CL does NOT attempt to read historical deposit contract logs (which would fail after history expiry). 4. Check for any code paths that still reference the deposit contract log method. 5. Test: process a deposit after the EL has pruned pre-merge history.
executable_checks: Process validator deposit after history expiry, verify success via EIP-6110
Verify no code path reads deposit contract logs post-history-expiry
Code audit: search for legacy deposit log reading code
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-EIP7927-ACT-INV-002. Invariant falsification. Related assumption: ASSUM-EIP7927-03. Missing EIP-6110 implementation combined with history expiry would halt all new validator activations.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for worst-case block size within 10 MiB gossip limit at 60M gas
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct an adversarial block maximizing serialized size within 60M gas: (a) maximum calldata (16 gas/byte non-zero, 4 gas/byte zero), (b) maximum contract creation initcode, (c) maximum LOG operations with data, (d) maximum RETURN data. 2. Measure the RLP-serialized size of the block. 3. Verify it is strictly < 10 MiB. 4. Try novel constructions: combine multiple size-maximizing strategies. 5. Account for: block header, transaction list overhead, uncle/ommers (should be empty post-merge). 6. If a construction exceeds 10 MiB, this is a critical finding: CL would reject valid EL blocks.
executable_checks: Construct max-calldata block at 60M gas, measure serialized size
Construct max-LOG-data block at 60M gas, measure serialized size
Verify all constructions produce size < 10 MiB
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-EIP7935-SECBND-INV-001. Boundary property. Related assumption: ASSUM-EIP7935-03. If violated, attacker produces valid EL blocks that CL rejects, causing consensus-execution layer split affecting all nodes. Requires PoC: construct a block within 60M gas whose serialized size >= 10 MiB.

checklist.title: Falsify blob_to_polynomial output dimension (FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB evaluation points)
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call blob_to_polynomial with a valid blob (FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB * 32 bytes). 2. Verify the output polynomial has exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB evaluation points. 3. Test with edge-case blobs: (a) all zeros, (b) all 0xFF (but valid field elements), (c) alternating pattern. 4. Verify the polynomial degree is at most FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB - 1. 5. Cross-check: compute cells from the polynomial and verify CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells are produced.
executable_checks: Verify blob_to_polynomial output length == FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB
Test with all-zero blob
Verify cell generation produces exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-ENCODE-POSTCOND-001. Post-condition falsification. Incorrect polynomial dimensions would produce invalid cells, causing DA failures.

checklist.title: Falsify Fiat-Shamir challenge determinism and collision resistance in batch verification
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Compute the Fiat-Shamir challenge r for a batch verification with specific (commitments, cell_indices, cells). 2. Modify one cell slightly and recompute r. Verify r changes. 3. Swap two commitments and recompute r. Verify r changes. 4. Test with duplicate commitments: verify they are included in the hash (not deduplicated). 5. Verify the hash domain separation includes all batch parameters. 6. Attempt to find two different inputs that produce the same challenge (collision search). 7. Verify the implementation matches the spec exactly (byte ordering, encoding).
executable_checks: Compute r, modify one cell, verify r changes
Test with duplicate commitments, verify they affect r
Verify implementation matches spec byte-for-byte
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-VERIFY-INV-001. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-PCS-FULU-04. Fiat-Shamir weakness allows proof forgery, enabling invalid cells to pass batch verification across all nodes.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for cell_index bounds validation from untrusted peers
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a batch verification request containing cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (one past valid range). 2. Send cell_index = 2^64 - 1. 3. Verify each is rejected before any root-of-unity lookup or array access. 4. Verify valid cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB - 1 is accepted. 5. Monitor for panics, segfaults, or index-out-of-bounds exceptions. 6. Check verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch for bounds checking on the cell_indices array.
executable_checks: Send cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, verify rejection
Send cell_index = MAX_UINT64, verify no crash
Verify cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB - 1 is accepted
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-SECBND-PRECOND-002. Boundary property. Trust boundary: untrusted P2P peer provides cell_indices. Out-of-bounds access in root-of-unity lookups could crash or corrupt the node.

checklist.title: Falsify Prague-Electra simultaneous activation at the same slot/block boundary
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify the EL Prague activation timestamp and CL Electra activation epoch map to the same slot. 2. Compute: expected_el_timestamp = GENESIS_TIME + (ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH * SECONDS_PER_SLOT). 3. Verify the EL client's Prague activation timestamp matches this value. 4. Test: process a block at the activation boundary. Verify both EL and CL transitions apply to the same block. 5. Test: what happens if there's a missed slot at the activation boundary? Verify both layers still activate correctly. 6. Cross-check across all client pairs (EL+CL combinations).
executable_checks: Verify EL Prague timestamp matches CL Electra epoch * SECONDS_PER_SLOT + GENESIS_TIME
Process block at activation boundary, verify both layers transition
Test missed slot at boundary, verify activation still occurs
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-EIP7600-FORK-INV-002. Invariant falsification. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7600-02. EL/CL fork activation mismatch would split the entire network.
